concepts.def: A tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons in shells.
Types of nuclear radiation with different penetration and ionising power.
Time for half the undecayed nuclei to decay.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nuclear Physics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nuclear Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nuclear Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Alpha particles are negatively charged.
Most of the atom is empty space with a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.
Electrons sit inside a uniform sphere of positive charge.
The nucleus occupies most of the atom's volume.

mcqs.q: After two half-lives, the fraction of the original nuclei still undecayed is:

options: grays (Gy)
becquerels (Bq)
sieverts (Sv)
joules (J)

mcqs.q: Energy is released in fission because:
options: Neutrons have no mass.
The fragments have a higher binding energy per nucleon than the original heavy nucleus.
Mass is created during the split.
The fragments have a lower binding energy per nucleon.

mcqs.q: Is a radioactive sample completely gone after two half-lives?
options: No — each half-life halves what remains, so one quarter is still undecayed after two half-lives.
Yes — all decay stops after one half-life.
They reflected off the shiny gold surface.
Yes — two halves make the whole sample decay.

mcqs.q: Why did some alpha particles bounce back in Rutherford's experiment?
options: They reflected off the shiny gold surface.
Yes — all decay stops after one half-life.
They approached a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus almost head-on and were repelled.
They collided with electrons spread throughout the atom.

mcqs.q: Is mass exactly conserved in nuclear reactions?
options: Yes — total mass never changes in any reaction.
They reflected off the shiny gold surface.
No — about half the mass disappears in every reaction.
No — a small mass difference (the mass defect) is converted to energy according to E = mc².

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Nuclear fission”?
options: A heavy nucleus such as uranium-235 splits into two lighter nuclei, releasing energy and neutrons.
The number of decays per second in a radioactive sample, measured in becquerels (Bq); A = λN.
The energy needed to separate a nucleus into its constituent nucleons; related to the mass defect by E = mc².
The probability per unit time that a given nucleus decays; appears in A = λN and N = N₀e^(−λt).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Activity”?
options: The probability per unit time that a given nucleus decays; appears in A = λN and N = N₀e^(−λt).
Alpha particles fired at gold foil mostly passed through, but a few rebounded — evidence for a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.
The average time taken for the number of undecayed nuclei in a sample, or its activity, to halve.
The number of decays per second in a radioactive sample, measured in becquerels (Bq); A = λN.
